---
title: Build a plugin
description: Choose between a remote (MCP) and a bundled (SDK) plugin, set up the repositories, and follow the path from first tool to marketplace listing.
icon: Hammer
---

A plugin connects PKU Harness to a campus service or adds a capability. The agent and the user use
it through the same typed tools, so the work is mostly: find the service's API, wrap it in good
tools, and (for bundled plugins) add native UI.

## Choose the kind

| | Remote plugin | Bundled plugin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Use for | Most contributions: public data, your own service, anything heavy | Things that need the device or the user's campus session: notifications, on-device data, authenticated campus APIs, native screens and widgets |
| Language | Any (MCP over Streamable HTTP) | TypeScript + zod + React Native |
| Release | Deploy your server; no app release | Ships with app releases (open an issue first) |
| Start from | [`templates/remote-plugin`](/docs/build/remote-plugin) | [`definePlugin`](/docs/build/bundled-plugin) |

## The path

<Steps>
<Step>

### Read the concepts

[Plugins](/docs/concepts/plugins), [Tools and effects](/docs/concepts/tools-and-effects),
[Permissions](/docs/concepts/permissions), [Security](/docs/concepts/security). They define the
rules every plugin follows.

</Step>
<Step>

### Find the protocol

If [`pkucli`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pkucli) already talks to the service, port it from there
and credit the file. See [Porting from pkucli](/docs/build/porting-from-pkucli).

</Step>
<Step>

### Write the tools

One tool per operation, honest effects, zod (or JSON Schema) inputs, descriptions written for the
model. See [Tools and schemas](/docs/build/tools).

</Step>
<Step>

### Add UI (bundled only)

Screens, Settings rows, dashboard widgets, slash commands. See [UI contributions](/docs/build/ui)
and [Languages](/docs/build/i18n).

</Step>
<Step>

### Test

`bun test` for pure logic, the mock model for the agent loop, the demo remote plugin for MCP.
See [Testing](/docs/build/testing).

</Step>
<Step>

### Publish

Register in the marketplace. See [Publishing](/docs/build/publishing) and the marketplace's
[manifest reference](/docs/marketplace/manifest) and [submit flow](/docs/marketplace/publishing).

</Step>
</Steps>

## Repositories you need

| Repository | You need it for |
| --- | --- |
| [`pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins) | The SDK, every bundled plugin, the registry, the remote template and examples. Start here. |
| [`pkuinfo/pku-harness`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness) | The app, to run your bundled plugin on a device or emulator. |
| [`pkuinfo/pkucli`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pkucli) | Reference implementations of PKU service protocols (Rust). |

```bash
mkdir pku-info && cd pku-info
git clone https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins.git     # SDK, plugins, registry, template
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness.git   # only to run bundled plugins in the app
cd pku-harness-plugins && bun install && bun test
```

<Callout title="No npm packages">
  The SDK and plugins are consumed from the GitHub repository, not npm. You work inside a checkout of
  `pku-harness-plugins` (its bun workspace and `tsconfig.json` resolve `@pku-harness/sdk` to
  `packages/sdk/src`); the app includes that repository as the git submodule `plugins/`. Remote
  plugins don't need the SDK at all.
</Callout>

<Callout type="info" title="Coming: declarative plugins">
  A third way, a plugin shared as a folder or link that the app interprets without an app release,
  is being designed. See [Declarative plugins (preview)](/docs/build/declarative-plugins).
</Callout>

## Ground rules (from CONTRIBUTING.md)

1. **Tools are the API.** Clear Chinese `title` (shown to users) and a `description` written for
   the model: when and how to use it. Validate input (zod for bundled, JSON Schema for MCP).
2. **Declare effects honestly.** Read-only tools set `readOnlyHint: true` (MCP) or `effect: 'read'`.
   Anything that changes state, spends money or posts publicly must say so.
3. **Never ask for campus passwords.** Credentials stay on the user's phone.
4. **Return data, not instructions.** Tool results are shown to the model as data.
5. **Declare `requires`.** Don't depend on a shell or filesystem on the phone.
6. **Port campus protocols from pkucli** where it already implements them, and credit the source.
7. **Be bilingual** (bundled plugins): English overlay for every user-facing manifest string, a
   `src/strings.ts` table for screen and widget text.
